definition: Affectivity refers to the positive and negative emotional side of a person’s experience. In this source, it is discussed as a factor linked with cognitive functioning and long-term cognitive decline.

reasons: The packet does not define affectivity as “the positive and negative emotional side of a person’s experience”; it only says that positive and negative affectivity are associated with cognitive function.
The wording “factor linked with cognitive functioning and long-term cognitive decline” is supported, but the broader definitional claim about what affectivity refers to is not.

The packet text does not provide a general definition of “affectivity” as the “positive and negative emotional side of a person’s experience.” It only uses the construct “positive and negative affectivity (PNA)” in relation to study outcomes.

The packet states that PNA is “significantly associated with cognitive function,” but it does not clearly state that affectivity is definitively a “factor linked with long-term cognitive decline.” Instead, it says “their relative strength of association with long-term cognitive decline remains unclear,” which does not support the definition’s claim about linkage to long-term decline.
